Comments: No evidence found of electoral register integration with government data exchange in Zimbabwe. ZEC (Zimbabwe Electoral Commission) systems appear entirely siloed.

revised_comments: Zimbabwe's voters' roll remains administered by the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission, but government plans announced by the Minister of Home Affairs and Cultural Heritage in early 2026 and debated in Parliament as Constitutional Amendment Bill No. 3 would transfer custody of the voters' roll to the Registrar-General's Office and link it to the Zimbabwe Population Registry System (ZPPRS). The ZPPRS centralises civil registration data and would allow automatic, real-time updates to voter eligibility as citizens reach voting age or are recorded as deceased. As of mid-2026 this requires a constitutional amendment that has not yet been enacted, so integration remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No evidence found of employment services integration with data exchange in Zimbabwe. NSSA (National Social Security Authority) has limited digital capability.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Fast-path check surfaced an authoritative Government of Zimbabwe/ILO National Action Plan (2022-2025) for the Labour Market Information System, which explicitly documents that employment/labour-market data are fragmented across the Ministry of Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare, ZIMSTAT, ZIMRA and NSSA, with no integrated LMIS and no inter-agency data-sharing policy. Per routing rules this moved the row from fast path to full path; fetched and read the ILO-hosted document in full, plus a 2026 follow-up article on NSSA's digital transformation corroborating continued fragmentation. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated) on the exchange-func-employment scale.
revised_comments: Zimbabwe's employment-services data remain fragmented across several bodies — the Ministry of Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare, ZIMSTAT, the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority and the National Social Security Authority (NSSA) — with no integrated Labour Market Information System (LMIS) linking job-seeker, unemployment or public-employment data into a shared government data exchange. The Government of Zimbabwe/ILO National Action Plan for Strengthening the LMIS (2022-2025) identifies the absence of a central repository, weak inter-agency coordination, and the absence of any data-sharing policy among labour-market data producers as key constraints. NSSA offers an online self-service contribution portal, but this is a standalone system rather than a cross-government exchange, and 2026 reporting on NSSA's digital transformation confirms that integration remains uneven and incomplete.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence found of AI/analytics integrated into Zimbabwe's government data exchange operations. Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan and National ICT Policy 2022-2027 do not reference AI deployment in data exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The two originally cited sources (UNCTAD eTrade Readiness Assessment, World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic) were fetched and re-read; neither contains AI-specific content, so they do not actually support a score either way. Fresh full-path searches found strong evidence that PRAZ's electronic Government Procurement (eGP) system, live since January 2024, uses AI for bid evaluation and fraud-detection analytics and is integrated with the tax, payment and companies-registry systems (Herald, September 2025, quoting PRAZ's ICT Director directly) — evidence of AI functioning across at least two integrated government systems. Also found Zimbabwe's National AI Strategy (2026-2030, launched March 2026), which plans a federated cross-ministry 'National AI and Data Platform' but is still at an early implementation stage, and an academic case study piloting machine-learning fraud detection at POTRAZ. Recalculated to 4 (Functional across at least 2 systems) on the strength of the PRAZ eGP evidence, but flagging for human review: it is not certain whether PRAZ's eGP-tax-payment-registry integration should count as part of the country's central 'data exchange' system as scoped by this indicator, or is better treated as a sector-specific procurement platform with bilateral integrations that falls outside strict scope.
revised_comments: Zimbabwe has begun applying artificial intelligence within specific government administrative platforms rather than across a single unified national data exchange. The Procurement Regulatory Authority of Zimbabwe (PRAZ) reports that its electronic Government Procurement (eGP) system, operational since January 2024, now uses AI-assisted bid evaluation and chatbot/virtual-assistant tools alongside analytics for fraud detection, and is integrated with the national payment system, the tax system and the deeds and companies registry. A National AI Strategy (2026-2030), launched in March 2026, sets out plans for a federated National AI and Data Platform intended to enable cross-ministry data sharing via privacy-preserving APIs, alongside sector-level AI pilots such as machine-learning-based fraud detection studied at POTRAZ. AI use within the core cross-government data exchange, as distinct from these sector-specific systems, is still emerging.
